summary: The fault is confidently localized inside auth-service's own two-change window — deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0, 14:00Z) and signing-key rotation cfg-2705 (14:01Z), both live and unrolled-back — with a clean, ramp-free error-rate step at exactly 14:02:00Z, while infra, traffic, resource and shared-dependency explanations are all excluded. But the origin cannot be separated between the two surviving hypotheses: H2 (key rotation before key material was fully effective, confidence 0.46) and H1 (jjwt 0.11→0.12 / TokenValidator rewrite, confidence 0.40) remain a near coin-flip, because the per-replica/per-pod dimensions, rollout fractions, and per-pod key-load fields that would discriminate them do not exist in this environment. Compounding this, the single quantitative anchor (the 36% error_rate) is labelled '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)' on both auth-service and api-gateway, while the reported symptom is 401 invalid_token (4xx), and no 4xx/status-class counter exists anywhere — so the link between the verified 5xx surge and the reported 401 surge is unverified. H3 (shared dependency) and H4/H5 are rejected on the evidence. Recommendation is a safe, reversible mitigation of the later change first, plus the specific discriminators (a 4xx/401 counter, per-pod version/key telemetry, log pipeline restoration) that would close the gap.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Scheduled signing-key rotation cfg-2705 (k-2025-10→k-2026-04) went live before key material was fully loaded
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The security-automation key rotation at 14:01Z flipped jwt.signing.key_id to k-2026-04, but the corresponding key material/JWKS state was not uniformly effective across auth-service's validation path, so a stable fraction of otherwise-valid tokens fail as invalid_token. Origin is the key-material/config state. First fix: revert/hold the rotation (point key_id back to k-2025-10, or dual-publish both keys) rather than roll back the deploy. Nudged slightly above H1 because it is the later of the two changes (closer to the 14:02Z onset), requires no pod restart (consistent with F17 restarts=0), and is the one change whose prior near-identical incident (HIST-108) presented the exact same symptom.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2705 flips auth-service jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 at 14:01:00Z; it is the only config change anywhere in 48h.
The new key id becomes effective before all validation paths hold the matching key material, so a fraction of valid tokens (e.g. those signed under the other key version) fail validation.
The resulting invalid_token fraction steps abruptly at 14:02Z — exactly 1 minute after the rotation and 2 minutes after the deploy — with no ramp.
No revert of the rotation occurred, so the plateau persists ~1h55m.

assumptions: Key material for k-2026-04 was not effective on all validation paths at cutover — cfg-2705 is recorded only as a single global service-level flip with no per-pod load/effective timestamp (F34), so this hop is not directly observable.
The ~1/3 fraction is a key-propagation effect rather than a partial code rollout (rollout fraction is not exposed anywhere — F32/F33/F36).
The 14:02Z 5xx-labelled step (F28) is driven by, or co-moves with, the reported 401 invalid_token symptom (F19); no 401/4xx counter exists on auth-service (F27).

ranked_hypotheses.title: auth-service deploy dep-5710 (jjwt 0.11→0.12 breaking parser API + TokenValidator rewrite) rejects valid tokens
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The auth-service v7.3.0 release that upgraded jjwt 0.11→0.12 (a documented breaking parser API change) and rewrote TokenValidator introduced a validation defect (changed clock-skew/claim/parser defaults) so that a stable subset of otherwise-valid tokens are rejected as invalid_token. Origin is the newly deployed code. First fix: roll back dep-5710. Held just below H2: it is the earlier of the two changes (2 minutes before onset vs 1), and a parser/validator code change would normally be accompanied by pod restarts, yet restarts are 0 across the window (F17) — an observation that mildly disfavours a code-rollout mechanism and mildly favours a restart-free config change.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0, jjwt 0.11->0.12 breaking parser API, TokenValidator rewritten) shipped at 14:00:00Z, live, never rolled back.
The new jjwt 0.12 parser / rewritten validator changes validation behaviour, rejecting tokens that the old parser accepted.
Rejected tokens surface as the failure fraction that steps at 14:02Z and plateaus immediately.
No rollback occurred, so the failure persists ~1h55m.

assumptions: The rewritten TokenValidator / jjwt 0.12 actually mis-validates a fraction of tokens — no logs are available (identity-namespace log pipeline down) to confirm a parser-error path.
A partial fraction arises from token shapes/claims exercising the changed code, not from partial rollout (no rollout fraction exposed — F32/F33/F36).
The 36% 5xx-labelled metric (F19) is dominated by, or co-moves with, the reported 401s.

ranked_hypotheses.title: auth-service is the victim of a shared downstream dependency (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A fault in a component shared on auth-service's path (redis-cache, the only shared component, or an unlisted IdP/secret-store/service-mesh) degrades token validation, with auth-service only surfacing 401s. Origin is outside auth-service. Now largely rejected: the decisive telemetry test the prior critique flagged as never-run was in fact carried out — all three other redis-cache consumers show flat error and latency series across the 14:02Z onset.
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: redis-cache (shared dependency) / unlisted IdP or secret-store

causal_chain.claim: auth-service -> redis-cache (cache, shared=true), the only shared component on its path; four consumers total.
redis-cache (or another shared/unlisted dependency) degrades at ~14:02Z, causing token lookups to surface as invalid_token on auth-service only.
Measurements contradict the premise: portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service show NO error-rate step and NO latency step at 14:02Z.
No change exists on redis-cache or its consumers in the window, and past redis incidents presented as latency, not 401s.

assumptions: An unlisted IdP/secret-store/service-mesh could still have changed despite no change record being visible for such services.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The critical telemetry test has now been run: all three other consumers of the shared redis-cache show flat error_rate and flat latency_p99 across 13:55-14:10Z (F42-F45), so the shared dependency is demonstrably not producing failures. Combined with no change on redis-cache or any consumer (F4/F22/F23), past redis incidents presenting as latency not 401s (F25), and the fault being confined to auth-service's own change window (F3/F8/F22), a shared-dependency origin is excluded. Residual risk only from unlisted IdP/secret-store components, which have no change record either.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Partial infrastructure failure: a subset of replicas/nodes/zone unhealthy (sidecar crash, clock skew)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A subset of auth-service replicas or co-tenant nodes is unhealthy (sidecar crash, node clock skew producing not-yet-valid/expired tokens), independent of the two auth-service changes.

causal_chain.claim: A subset of replicas/nodes is unhealthy, so only a fraction of validations fail.
Mechanism: sidecar crash / clock skew yields invalid_token on those replicas.
No infra event, restart or resource anomaly is visible to corroborate it.

assumptions: Some replicas/nodes failed independently of the two auth-service changes.
Clock skew exists (no clock-skew metric is exposed — F26).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: F17 shows zero restarts and flat cpu/memory/latency/rate-limiting across the onset; F3/F7 show no infra or node change in the window; F15 shows a perfectly sustained plateau inconsistent with partial-node flapping; the onset is a clean single 14:02Z step aligned to the auth-service changes. Retained at floor confidence only because per-replica/per-zone evidence is unobtainable (F26/F27).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Reporting artifact: the 36% error rate is skewed by the down identity-namespace log pipeline
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The magnitude and timing of the 36% are artifacts of the identity-namespace log pipeline outage, so the true onset may predate this morning.

causal_chain.claim: Log pipeline for identity namespace is down, so auth-service logs are unavailable.
The measured error rate is skewed by that outage.

assumptions: The metric backend is affected by the log pipeline outage.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: F18 shows auth-service metric queries return complete data (partial:false, missing_points:0) from the metrics backend independent of the log pipeline; F13/F28 show a clean 0.16->36.08 step in a single 60s bucket at 14:02Z with a sustained plateau; F30 shows an independent simultaneous step on api-gateway. Magnitude and onset are real, not coverage artifacts.

facts.statement: Across the full 48h window (2026-04-13T16:00Z to 2026-04-15T16:00Z) exactly two auth-service changes occurred near onset: deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0, 'Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation', changes 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten') at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z, status live, rolled_back_at null; and config change cfg-2705 ('Scheduled signing-key rotation', author security-automation) flipping jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04 at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z.

The two changes are one minute apart and both precede incident onset; the key rotation is the later of the two, so key_id k-2026-04 went live one minute after the new TokenValidator/jjwt 0.12 parser shipped.

The only other deployment in the 48h window is market-data-service dep-5699 (v5.0.3) at 2026-04-15T11:35:00Z, ~2.5 hours before onset; no deploy or config change is recorded for redis-cache or any of its consumers in the incident window.

auth-service error_rate steps in a single 60s bucket from 0.16 (last normal, 14:01Z) to 36.08 at 2026-04-15T14:02:00Z with no ramp-up, and holds a stable plateau of ~34.4-38.5 through the end of data (~1h55m, 15:55Z avg 36.27).

auth-service request_rate is flat across the onset (~386-408 req/s) and resource metrics are flat: cpu_pct ~37-38%, memory_pct ~51-53%, latency_p99_ms ~88-91ms, restarts 0 for every bucket 12:00-15:50Z, rate_limited_per_min ~2/min unchanged.

auth-service's own metrics query returns complete data (partial:false, missing_points:0, 240 points) from the metrics backend, so the ~36% figure is not a coverage artifact of the down identity-namespace log pipeline.

The auth-service error_rate metric is explicitly labelled '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)', i.e. it counts 5xx responses, whereas the reported symptom is 401 invalid_token, a 4xx; auth-service exposes no 4xx/status-class or invalid_token counter (four status-class/group-by metric queries returned not_found).

api-gateway (the sole upstream caller of auth-service) shows a simultaneous but lower step, from 0.19 at 14:01:00Z to ~20.2-22.1 at 14:02:00Z, sustaining ~20.6-21.9; this series carries the same '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)' label and api-gateway likewise exposes no 4xx/status-class metric.

auth-service exposes only seven metrics (cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, rate_limited_per_min, request_rate, restarts) with no pod/replica/instance/node/zone/route dimension and no per-status-class counter; grouped-dimension queries were rejected as not_found, so per-replica error rates cannot be produced.

The deployment record for dep-5710 carries only service-level instant fields (id, service, version, deployed_at, author, summary, changes, status, rolled_back_at) with no rollout-fraction, replica-count, canary, percentage or per-pod version field, and no hidden second/canary rollout record exists near onset.
The cfg-2705 config-change record is service-level and timestamp-only with no per-instance or per-pod 'loaded'/JWKS-propagation timeline, so no staggered key propagation is observable in change data.

redis-cache is the only shared component on auth-service's path (shared=true, four consumers: auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service), has zero config changes in the 48h window and zero deployments, and a past redis-cache-side incident (HIST-107) presented as latency/cache-miss symptoms on market-data-service, not 401s.

All three other redis-cache consumers show flat error_rate across 13:55-14:10Z (portfolio-service 0.11-0.32, pricing-engine 0.11-0.29, market-data-service 0.1-0.32; all with complete data), and flat latency_p99 (portfolio-service 169-192ms, pricing-engine 56.98-65.89ms, market-data-service 37.38-43.25ms), so the shared cache is not producing failures for its other consumers.

Historical precedents are leads only: HIST-108 (2025-10-01) '401s after JWT signing key rotation' was caused by key rotation publishing a new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS; HIST-109 (2025-07-11) was 401s after a JWT library upgrade changing clock-skew default.
user-db exposes no error_rate metric (db-type metrics only) and kyc-provider has no telemetry, so those two dependencies cannot be error-tested directly; kyc-provider's sole caller is auth-service.

assumptions: ASSUMPTION: The reported 401 'invalid_token' symptom and the verified ~36% 5xx-labelled error_rate step at 14:02Z are the same event (i.e. the 5xx series is dominated by, or co-moves with, the 401 failures). No 4xx/401 counter exists on any service and logs are unsearchable, so this is assumed, not verified.

ASSUMPTION (H2): Key material for k-2026-04 was not effective on all of auth-service's validation paths at cutover, producing the stable ~1/3 failure fraction. cfg-2705 is recorded only as a single global service-level flip with no per-pod load/effective timestamp, so this hop is not directly observable.

ASSUMPTION (H1): The rewritten TokenValidator under jjwt 0.12 actually mis-validates a fraction of otherwise-valid tokens (e.g. changed clock-skew/claim/parser defaults). No logs are available to confirm a parser-error path.

ASSUMPTION (both): The ~1/3 failure fraction reflects a partial effect (key-propagation lag or token-shape-dependent code path) rather than a partial code rollout; the rollout fraction is not exposed anywhere.

ASSUMPTION: The api-gateway ~21% step is a downstream consequence of auth-service token-validation failures rather than an independent gateway-side fault; the gateway's lower magnitude is attributed to its traffic mix only partly consisting of token-validation calls.

ASSUMPTION: No change occurred in an unlisted IdP, secret-store, ingress/service-mesh, or config-store component during the window; no change record is visible for such services, but their existence/inventory coverage is unverified.
ASSUMPTION: The 14:02Z onset is caused by one (or both) of the two recorded auth-service changes rather than by an unrecorded event; the change inventory is assumed complete for the window.

timeline.event: auth-service deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0) lands: 'Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation', changes 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten'. Status live, no rollback.
Scheduled signing-key rotation cfg-2705 (author security-automation) flips auth-service jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04 — one minute after the deploy.
Last normal auth-service error_rate bucket: 0.16 (60s resolution).

auth-service error_rate steps in a single 60s bucket to 36.08, with no ramp-up, and holds a ~34.4-38.5 plateau. api-gateway steps simultaneously from 0.19 to ~20.7 (same % of requests (HTTP 5xx) label).
All three other redis-cache consumers (portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service) show no error-rate or latency step across 13:55-14:10Z, refuting a shared-cache-origin fault.
Incident INC-007 reported (SEV-1): ~a third of token validations fail with 401 invalid_token; auth-service error rate ~36%.
Confirmed auth-service exposes only seven aggregate metrics with no pod/replica/zone dimension and no 4xx or invalid_token counter; per-replica breakdown is unobtainable.
auth-service error_rate still elevated: 15:55Z avg 36.27 (max 38.23); spike sustained ~1h55m with no recovery.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately mitigate the later of the two changes: revert/hold the key rotation cfg-2705 by pointing jwt.signing.key_id back to k-2025-10, or better, dual-publish/dual-accept both k-2025-10 and k-2026-04 in the JWKS so tokens signed under either key validate. Do not roll back dep-5710 first. Watch auth-service error_rate (and api-gateway error_rate) at 60s resolution for a drop from the ~36% plateau.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 is the top-ranked hypothesis (0.46) and the rotation is the later, restart-free change closest to the 14:02Z onset (F2/F9/F28); the past near-identical incident HIST-108 was fixed by resolving key-material/JWKS propagation (F6/F11). Dual-publish is low-risk and reversible, and is the safest diagnostic: if the rate drops, H2 is confirmed; if it does not, the change can be reverted.

recommended_actions.action: If and only if the key-rotation revert/dual-publish does not reduce the error rate within a few minutes, roll back dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0 -> previous version), since it is the other live change in the onset window and the only remaining candidate.
recommended_actions.rationale: H1 (jjwt 0.11->0.12 breaking parser API + TokenValidator rewrite) is the other surviving origin at 0.40 confidence and the deploy remains live with no rollback (F1/F7); a rollback is the discriminating mitigation and HIST-109 shows a JWT-library regression with the same symptom class (F11).

recommended_actions.action: Instrument a 4xx/status-class counter (or an invalid_token counter) on auth-service and api-gateway and add per-pod/per-replica/per-zone dimensions to the error metrics, so the reported 401 symptom can be measured directly rather than inferred from a 5xx-labelled series.
recommended_actions.rationale: The single quantitative anchor (36%) is measured on a series labelled '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)' while the symptom is 401 invalid_token (4xx); no 4xx counter or per-replica dimension exists on either service (F19/F26/F27/F38/F39). Without this, neither the symptom link nor the partial-fraction mechanism can be verified.

recommended_actions.action: Restore the identity-namespace log pipeline (separate ticket) and confirm the failure by grepping auth-service logs for invalid_token / JWKS-load / key-id / parser exceptions across 14:00-14:15Z; capture the offending error signature per instance.
recommended_actions.rationale: Logs are the only source that could show whether failures are JWKS key-load lag (H2), a jjwt 0.12 parser/claim behaviour change (H1), or clock skew — none of which are observable in metrics or change data (gap: identity-namespace pipeline down since morning).

recommended_actions.action: After mitigation, verify recovery against the plateau baseline: confirm auth-service error_rate returns to the ~0.21% baseline and api-gateway to ~0.22-0.27%, sustained for at least 30-60 minutes, before declaring the incident resolved.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pre-onset baselines are well established (F13/F14/F30/F37), and the plateau was stable and sustained for ~1h55m (F15/F29), so a return to baseline is a clean, measurable recovery signal.

recommended_actions.action: Emit key material and JWKS before (or atomically with) the jwt.signing.key_id flip, and/or perform key rotations as staged dual-publish across pods with a per-pod effective-key health check; add a canary/staged rollout strategy with per-instance version and error telemetry for auth-service deploys.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-108 was caused by a key id published before all pods loaded the JWKS (F6/F11), and the absence of any rollout-fraction or per-pod key-load telemetry (F32-F36) is what made this incident undecidable; adding both ordering guarantees and observability prevents recurrence and enables fast discrimination next time.

recommended_actions.action: Replace the shared 5xx-labelled error_rate contract with a status-class-decomposed SLI across all services, so 4xx (including 401) and 5xx are separately visible; standardise this in the metric schema.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 5xx-vs-4xx mismatch (F19/F38) blocked the quantitative anchor from measuring the reported symptom on either auth-service or api-gateway, and no status-class metric exists on any queried service (F27/F39) — a systemic observability gap that would obscure future auth-class outages.

data_gaps: auth-service logs are unsearchable (identity-namespace log pipeline down since this morning), so it is unknown which pods/replicas rejected tokens and which error path (JWKS key-load lag, jjwt 0.12 parser/claim behaviour, clock skew) produced each 401.

No per-replica/per-pod/instance/node/zone dimension exists on auth-service (only 7 aggregate metrics; grouped queries returned not_found), so the core H1-vs-H2 discriminator — uniform service-wide failure fraction vs a subset of replicas — cannot be measured.

No 4xx/status-class or invalid_token counter exists on auth-service or api-gateway (four status-class metric names returned not_found on the gateway; none on auth-service), so the link between the verified 36% 5xx surge and the reported 401 surge is unverified.

No rollout-fraction, canary percentage, per-instance/pod version, or per-pod key_id/JWKS-load field exists in the deployment or config schemas, so partial rollout versus staggered key propagation cannot be distinguished from version/key data.
user-db exposes no error_rate metric (db-type metrics only) and kyc-provider has no telemetry, so those two dependencies could not be error-tested; kyc-provider's sole caller is auth-service.

redis-cache's own health metrics (hit_ratio_pct, evictions_per_min, cpu_pct, connected_clients) in 13:55-14:10Z were not queried (budget exhausted), so the H3 refutation rests on the three consumer services being clean rather than on cache-side metrics.

No change records are visible for secret/key-management, ingress/service-mesh, or config-store components; it is unverified whether such services exist in inventory or simply lack a change feed, so an unlisted IdP/secret-store/ingress change cannot be fully excluded.
Per-replica, per-route, and per-pod topology (including whether dep-5710 had a staged rollout) is absent from the dependency graph, which carries one has_telemetry boolean per node only.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: A reduction in the auth-service error_rate immediately after reverting/holding cfg-2705 (or dual-publishing both keys) would confirm H2 as the origin; failure to improve would shift the conclusion to H1 (dep-5710) and make the deploy rollback the correct fix.

A direct 4xx/401 (invalid_token) counter on auth-service or api-gateway stepping at 14:02:00Z at ~36% would confirm the 5xx-labelled error_rate genuinely measures the reported symptom; a 5xx-only step with a flat 4xx series would indicate the reported 401s are a separate or additional problem and that the current anchor does not measure the symptom at all.

auth-service logs (once the identity pipeline is restored) showing JWKS key-load failures / unknown-key-id errors would favour H2; showing parser/claim/clock-skew exceptions under jjwt 0.12 would favour H1.

Per-replica error data (if the metric backend ever exposed a pod/replica dimension) showing the ~36% concentrated in a subset of replicas would favour a partial-rollout or per-pod key-load mechanism; a uniform fraction across all replicas would favour a deterministic code/parser behaviour effect (H1) or a globally incorrect key state (H2).

Evidence of key rotation applying before key material was effective (e.g. a JWKS endpoint serving only k-2026-04 while k-2026-04 material was not loaded on some pods) would confirm H2's mechanism; conversely, evidence that both key ids validate correctly on all pods would exclude H2.

Discovery of a change in an unlisted IdP, secret-store, ingress/service-mesh or config-store component at ~14:00-14:02Z would reopen H3 (shared/upstream dependency origin) and change the localization away from auth-service's own two changes.

findings.statement: A single auth-service deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0) landed at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z, ~12 minutes before the reported onset (14:12), still live with no rollback; it upgraded the JWT library and rewrote token validation.
A scheduled signing-key rotation cfg-2705 changed auth-service jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04 at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z, one minute after the deploy and ~11 minutes before onset.

Full-window inventory across all services shows only two changes around onset-or-earlier: dep-5710 (auth-service, 14:00) and cfg-2705 (auth-service, 14:01); the only other deploy, dep-5699 market-data-service v5.0.3 at 11:35, is ~2.5 hours before onset.

No deployments occurred for the shared redis-cache (0 in window), and redis-cache is shared with three other services (portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service), so a redis-cache-side change is not present in deployment data and a redis fault would be expected to hit those consumers too.

auth-service error_rate (unit: '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)') jumps abruptly from a ~0.2% baseline to ~36% at the 14:02Z bucket. The last normal bucket is 14:00Z (avg 0.21, max 0.26); the next 2-minute bucket 14:02Z is 37.21 avg / 38.34 max. No ramp-up is visible in the 2-minute buckets before 14:02Z.

In the 5-minute view the error_rate onset is covered by the 14:00Z bucket (avg 22.21, max 38.34) because that bucket only partially includes the post-onset minutes; the surrounding baseline buckets (13:50-13:55Z) are 0.21 and 0.26 avg, and the plateau from 14:05Z onward is ~35.6-37.2 avg.
The elevated failure rate persists to the end of data: 15:55Z avg 36.27 (max 38.23), and the whole window mean is 17.89 — i.e. the spike is sustained, not a transient blip, for ~1h55m.
auth-service request_rate is flat across the onset (all buckets ~386-408 req/s; 13:55Z avg 395.17, 14:00Z avg 401.35, 14:05Z avg 398.11), so the error surge is not explained by a traffic increase.

Resource metrics on auth-service are flat through the onset: cpu_pct stays ~37-38% (14:00Z avg 38.81), memory_pct ~51-53% (14:00Z avg 52.06), latency_p99_ms ~88-91ms (14:00Z avg 89.92, maximum in whole window 101.03), restarts are 0 for every bucket 12:00-15:50Z, and rate_limited_per_min is ~2/min unchanged. This rules out CPU/memory pressure, restart loops, latency degradation and rate-limiting as the driver.

auth-service's own metrics query returns complete data (partial:false, missing_points:0, 240 total points) for error_rate/request_rate/cpu/memory with no warnings, so the ~36% figure is NOT a coverage artifact of the down identity-namespace log pipeline — it comes from the metrics backend, which is reporting normally for this service.

auth-service error_rate metric is explicitly labelled '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)', i.e. it measures 5xx responses; the incident is reported as 401 'invalid_token', which is a 4xx. The metric spike and the reported 401 symptom are therefore measured on different status classes — the 36% figure corroborates a large failure fraction but is not itself a direct count of 401s.

redis-cache re-queried with explicit direction/depth arguments returns a complete (partial:false, attempts:1) graph: redis-cache is shared=true, type redis, has_telemetry=true, and has exactly four consumers — auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service. So the earlier empty-edges result is superseded and the full consumer set of the shared cache is confirmed.

The redis-cache consumers are internal services with telemetry (portfolio-service/market-data-service/pricing-engine all has_telemetry:true, shared:false), and portfolio-service also writes to another shared store (ledger-db, shared:true) alongside redis-cache — so the shared-dependency surface for the identity path is not redis-cache alone: portfolio-service -> ledger-db and order/payment -> ledger-db, order/payment -> kafka are additional shared components (ledger-db, kafka, both shared:true) that are off auth-service's path.

auth-service is the sole service with a change inside the 13:30-15:59Z window: get_deployments for that window returns count 1 (dep-5710 auth-service v7.3.0 at 14:00:00Z, status live, rolled_back_at null), and get_config_changes returns count 1 (cfg-2705 auth-service jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 at 14:01:00Z). No deploy or config change is recorded for any redis-cache consumer or for redis-cache itself in the incident window.

redis-cache itself has zero config changes across the full 48h window (2026-04-13T16:00Z to 2026-04-15T16:00Z): get_config_changes scoped to service=redis-cache returns count 0, confirming a cache-side config/key change is not present in change data.

api-gateway fans out to six services over http (auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service, market-data-service, payment-service), so a gateway-side fault would be expected to raise errors across all of them, not on auth-service alone; the gateway's other callers (portfolio-service, order-service, payment-service) are not downstream of auth-service.

Historical precedent HIST-107 (2025-12-09) 'Cold cache storm after redis failover' affected [redis-cache, market-data-service] with 'cache miss storm' / 'quote latency' and was NOT a 401/auth story — so past redis-cache-side incidents presented as latency/miss symptoms on market-data-service, a different signature from the current 401 invalid_token pattern, and none of the six returned precedents is titled around 401s from a shared cache.

findings.statement: Auth-service exposes ONLY seven metrics — cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, rate_limited_per_min, request_rate, restarts. There is NO pod/replica/instance/node/zone/route dimension and no per-status-class counter available, so the metric backend cannot answer the H1-vs-H2 replication question with dimensions: every error_rate query returns a single aggregated series for the whole service.

No per-replica / per-pod breakdown is obtainable. Attempts to request grouped dimensions on auth-service were rejected as not_found (group_by pod,replica,instance,node,zone), and no 4xx-specific or invalid_token-specific metric exists on the service. Therefore the task's requested 'per-replica error-rate values' CANNOT be produced from this backend; the answer to 'uniform across all replicas vs subset of replicas' is not directly measurable here.

Using the finest available resolution (60s buckets), the auth-service error_rate onset is EXACTLY at 2026-04-15T14:02:00Z: the 14:01 bucket is 0.16 (last normal), and the very next bucket 14:02 jumps to 36.08, then holds 34.4-38.53 through 14:15. No ramp-up exists between 14:01 and 14:02. Note this 14:02 step is 1 minute AFTER the 14:01 key-rotation (cfg-2705) and 2 minutes after the 14:00 deploy (dep-5710).

The ~36% magnitude is stable across the whole window and is not a partial-rollout-cut artifact at the aggregate level: post-onset buckets are 36.08, 38.34, 36.22, 37.97, 38.53, 35.78, 35.84, 34.4, 34.92, 37.74, 36.74, 36.15, 37.97, 36.38 (means), i.e. ~34.4-38.5 with mean 24.51 over the truncated window. The service-level failure fraction settles immediately at its final plateau value rather than stepping up in stages.

api-gateway (the sole upstream caller of auth-service) shows a SIMULTANEOUS but LOWER error_rate onset: baseline ~0.22-0.27 through 13:59, then 14:01 avg 10.46 (max 20.72), plateauing at ~20.6-21.9 from 14:03 onward. So the gateway's own failure fraction (~21%) is roughly 0.58x of auth-service's (~36%), consistent with the gateway's traffic mix being only partly composed of token-validation calls to auth-service. This is a distinct series on a second service and it steps at the same time as auth-service.

redis-cache exposes an entirely different metric set (connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct) and has NO error_rate metric at all, confirming that component-type metric namespaces differ; a cache-side error metric would not appear under error_rate. This means the shared-dependency hypothesis H3 cannot be checked with an error_rate-style query against redis-cache and would need its own metric names.

The deployment inventory for auth-service returns a SINGLE deployment record for dep-5710 with service-level, instant fields only — id, service, version, deployed_at, author, summary, changes, status, rolled_back_at — and NO rollout-fraction, replica-count, per-instance, canary, percentage, or per-pod version field. dep-5710 = v7.3.0, deployed_at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z, status 'live', rolled_back_at null. Therefore no rollout-fraction/per-instance version evidence exists for v7.3.0 vs the prior version at 14:02Z-14:15Z.

An unscoped (all-services) deployment query over 13:50-14:20Z returns count 1 and the same single dep-5710 record — no additional per-version or per-replica deployment entries appear anywhere near onset, so there is no hidden second rollout (e.g. a canary group record) for auth-service v7.3.0 in this window.

The config-change record for cfg-2705 is also service-level and timestamp-only: it reports key 'jwt.signing.key_id', old_value 'k-2025-10' -> new_value 'k-2026-04' at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z and carries NO per-instance or per-pod 'loaded' timestamp or key-propagation/JWKS-load timeline. The only key_id change is this single global flip, so there is no observable lag/stagger in key propagation across pods in the change data.

auth-service is registered with shared=false and its dependency graph is one caller-independent service node with three downstream edges (user-db, redis-cache, kyc-provider) — the graph carries a single 'has_telemetry' boolean per node and no per-replica or per-pod topology, so dependency data cannot supply instance-level version or key-load information either.

Inference: because no backend exposes a rollout-fraction, per-instance version, or per-pod key_id/load field, the '~1/3 of token validations fail' magnitude cannot be sourced to a partial/canary rollout from the available data — dep-5710 must be treated as recorded only as a single whole-service v7.3.0 deployment at 14:00:00Z, and neither H1's subset-of-replicas mechanism nor H2's per-pod JWKS-lag mechanism is confirmable from rollout/version data.

api-gateway error_rate at 60s resolution steps from 0.19 at 14:01:00Z to 20.72 at 14:02:00Z and plateaus at 20.18-22.05 through 14:10Z; summary min 0.17, max 22.05, missing_points 0, partial:false. The step is exactly simultaneous with the auth-service 14:02 onset and of the same abrupt (no-ramp) character.

The api-gateway error_rate series carries the same unit label as auth-service's: '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)'. So the ~21% F30 step is, by the metric's own definition, a fraction of 5xx responses — NOT a 4xx/401 count passed through from auth-service.

api-gateway exposes ONLY six metrics — cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts — with no status-class, 4xx, 5xx-breakdown, requests-by-status or http_4xx series. Four independent status-class metric queries (error_rate_4xx, status_class_4xx, requests_by_status, http_4xx) all return not_found with the same six-metric available_metrics list. Therefore api-gateway provides NO 4xx/status-class series that could step at 14:02Z at the auth-service 36% magnitude, and the anchor remains unconfirmed on the 4xx-admixture question.

The gateway step magnitude (~20.2-22.1 avg) does NOT match the auth-service magnitude (~34.4-38.5, F29) at the same 14:02Z onset. It is ~0.56-0.58x of auth-service's level (20.72/36.08 at 14:02), consistent with F30: the gateway's mix only partly consists of token-validation calls fanned out to auth-service, so no 4xx series at the auth-service 36% magnitude exists on api-gateway.

The gateway's 5xx-labelled failure fraction persists at the same plateau long after onset: 14:15Z avg 20.29, 14:17Z avg 21.09, 14:19Z avg 21.94 (missing_points 0), matching F30's sustained ~20.6-21.9 plateau rather than a transient. Because the label is 5xx, the sustained ~21% is a 5xx fraction on the gateway and does not by itself count the reported 401 invalid_token responses.

portfolio-service (a redis-cache consumer) shows NO error-rate step across 13:55-14:10Z: every 60s bucket sits between 0.11 and 0.32, with the 14:02Z bucket at 0.12 and the pre-onset buckets 13:55-14:01Z at 0.12-0.32. Data is complete (missing_points:0, total_points:16, partial:false).

pricing-engine (a redis-cache consumer) shows NO error-rate step across 13:55-14:10Z: values range 0.11-0.29 with the 14:02Z bucket at 0.19; post-onset buckets (14:03-14:10Z) stay 0.15-0.29. Complete data (missing_points:0, total_points:16).
market-data-service (a redis-cache consumer) shows NO error-rate step across 13:55-14:10Z: values range 0.1-0.32 with the 14:02Z bucket at 0.12. Complete data (missing_points:0, total_points:16).

Latency_p99 on all three redis-cache consumers is flat across the onset with no step at ~14:02Z: portfolio-service 169-192ms (14:02Z = 174.97), pricing-engine 56.98-65.89ms (14:02Z = 63.69), market-data-service 37.38-43.25ms (14:02Z = 42.21). All three complete (missing_points:0).

user-db does not expose an error_rate metric (it exposes db-type metrics only: connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min), so the requested error-metric check on user-db cannot be performed as specified.
kyc-provider has no telemetry at all, so it cannot be tested for errors or latency directly; its sole caller is auth-service.
